sections.heading: What the radar shows here
sections.text: The circle averages -7.93 dB in HH and -17.26 dB in HV. Built-up land is the brightest type, at 1.29 dB in HH, and smooth bare ground the darkest, at -22.14 dB in HV.

sections.heading: Terrain types and what they mean
sections.text: Changing fields, 24.35 km2, are the plots whose HV moved most during the season; on this date they sit at -16.7 dB in HV and -9.96 dB in HH. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes, 22.6% of the circle, give the strongest HV, -14.61 dB, from leaves and branches. Smooth bare ground, 49.29 km2, is dark in both channels, -16.2 dB in HH, because dry, smooth soil reflects the pulse away.

sections.heading: Data quality notes
sections.text: No flag applies on this date. One track only, so field edges facing away from the radar can look darker. Possible cause of the brighter changing fields on this date: crops still standing before the summer harvest; harvest records would check it.
